title: FPGA-CC: Confidential Containers for Virtualized FPGAs
problem: Virtualized FPGA cloud services lack security mechanisms to protect user data and computation, as current trusted execution environment (TEE) approaches do not support FPGA acceleration in cloud environments.
motivation: Growing adoption of FPGAs in cloud computing for performance-critical workloads creates security vulnerabilities; TEE-based confidential computing lacks FPGA support, requiring new security architecture.
method: FPGA-CC creates a secure channel connecting virtualized FPGAs (specialized computing hardware running on shared cloud servers) to a trusted execution environment or TEE (a secure CPU that encrypts code and data from other users). This isolated data path protects information as it flows between the FPGA and the secure CPU, keeping everything confidential from other users on the same cloud. The framework achieves this while maintaining acceptable performance for real applications.
key_novelty: FPGA-CC is the first to make virtualized FPGAs secure for cloud users by connecting them through an encrypted channel to trusted CPU environments that protect the data traveling between them.
contributions: End-to-end confidential container architecture for virtualized FPGAs
Secure communication path between TEE-enabled CPU and virtualized FPGA resources
Demonstrates practical security implementation with acceptable performance overhead
baselines: standard virtualized FPGA approaches without TEE
limitations: Performance overhead of security mechanisms not quantified in abstract; limited to specific cloud FPGA platforms; scalability to larger clusters not addressed.
primary_theme: Secure confidential containers for virtualized FPGAs
